title: Shanaka's Stunning 23-Ball 58 Rescues Seattle Orcas from 72/6. India-Born Harmeet Singh Stars with Bat and Ball in MLC Win Over LA Knight Riders
excerpt: Former Sri Lanka captain smashes five fours and five sixes to lift Orcas from the brink; Mumbai-born spinner Harmeet Singh takes 2/20 and scores 19 in comfortable 20-run win at Oakland Coliseum
body:
When Shimron Hetmyer fell for 1, caught at slip off Sunil Narine in the fourth over, Seattle Orcas were 16 for 3 and staring at a total capitulation. Less than ten overs later, they were 72 for 6. Their top order had been dismantled by a disciplined LA Knight Riders attack. The contest, Match 14 of Major League Cricket 2026, appeared all but over.

Then Dasun Shanaka walked in and turned the game — and the evening at Oakland Coliseum — upside down.

The former Sri Lanka captain, playing his second MLC season with the Orcas, unleashed an innings of breathtaking power and calculation: **58 not out off just 23 balls**, with five fours and five sixes, a strike rate of 252. It was the kind of knock that makes franchise cricket worth watching — a player of international pedigree reaching into his deepest reserves when everything around him was collapsing.

## A Top-Order Meltdown

The Orcas' troubles began from ball one. Fabian Allen removed opener Shayan Jahangir in the first over, and Jason Holder had Matthew Breetzke caught behind soon after. When Narine struck twice — dismissing Hetmyer and later wicketkeeper Tim Seifert — Seattle had lost four wickets inside the powerplay for just 32 runs.

Ali Sheikh, the 23-year-old Pakistani-American all-rounder and former USA Under-19 captain, provided the first meaningful resistance. His counter-attacking 38 off 29 balls, featuring three fours and three sixes, at least ensured the Knight Riders' spinners could not bowl unchallenged. Captain Marcus Stoinis contributed a scratchy 10 off 19 at the other end before falling to Shadley van Schalkwyk, and when Sheikh was pinned lbw by Narine, the Orcas were 72 for 6 with less than seven overs remaining.



> **"## A Top-Order Meltdown

The Orcas' troubles began from ball one."**


## The Shanaka Storm

That was when Shanaka took charge. Partnering first with India-born left-arm spinner Harmeet Singh and then with Cameron Gannon, the 34-year-old tore into every bowler willing to offer width. Ali Khan, the Pakistan-born USA international, bore the brunt — his four overs leaked 50 runs. Shanaka added 41 with Harmeet Singh in just 23 balls and another 41 with Gannon in 18, dragging the Orcas to 154 for 7.


![Sunil Narine — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ee/Sunil_Narine.jpg)


Harmeet Singh himself contributed a handy 19 off 16 with two fours — a useful knock from number eight that extended the partnership long enough for Shanaka to go ballistic. The Mumbai-born spinner, who moved to the United States and became the first-ever number one domestic draft pick in MLC history, has quietly built a reputation as one of American cricket's most complete players.

## The Chase Falls Apart

Chasing a target that suddenly looked far more imposing than it had at the halfway mark, the Knight Riders started strongly. Colin Munro (33 off 36) and Andre Fletcher (23 off 13, five fours) put on 42 in the powerplay without loss.

But the wheels came off spectacularly when Fletcher fell to Jasdeep Singh, and one ball later, Unmukt Chand — the former India Under-19 World Cup-winning captain who represents one of the most fascinating diaspora stories in American cricket — was caught for a golden duck off Ottniel Baartman. At 43 for 2, the momentum had shifted entirely.

Harmeet Singh then struck twice, removing Saif Badar and later Munro, to peg LAKR back to 70 for 4. Stoinis picked up where his spin counterpart left off, dismissing Narine, Rovman Powell via a sharp Ali Sheikh catch, and finishing with the wickets of Jason Holder and Matthew Tromp in the final over to end with outstanding figures of **3 for 28 from four overs**. Harmeet's 4-0-20-2 was equally impressive — tidy, probing, and decisive during the middle overs when LAKR needed to accelerate.

The Knight Riders were eventually restricted to 134 for 8, losing by 20 runs.

## Cricket at the Coliseum

The match was played at the Oakland Coliseum, the former home of the Oakland Athletics baseball team, now repurposed as one of MLC's West Coast venues. For the thousands of South Asian fans in the Bay Area — many of them Indian and Pakistani Americans who grew up watching cricket thousands of miles away — the sight of international-quality T20 cricket at a venue they know from baseball season carries a particular thrill.

The result lifted the Orcas to three wins from six matches, pushing them to the top of the points table alongside the Texas Super Kings. LAKR, who had thrashed Seattle by 81 runs in their first meeting just six days earlier, now have two wins and two losses from four outings in what is shaping up to be the most competitive MLC season yet.

**Brief Scores:** Seattle Orcas 154/7 in 20 overs (Dasun Shanaka 58* off 23, Ali Sheikh 38, Harmeet Singh 19; Sunil Narine 4-1-17-2, Fabian Allen 4-0-18-2) beat LA Knight Riders 134/8 in 20 overs (Colin Munro 33, Andre Fletcher 23, Jason Holder 21; Marcus Stoinis 4-0-28-3, Harmeet Singh 4-0-20-2) by 20 runs.
